failures.criterion: AC1 / the section's trustworthiness — the new environment paragraph of "Anatomy of a Sandbox pod" tells the reader that a printenv inside the container finds none of the eleven variables in the table below it. That is false of PATH, the table's first row, and a reader disproves it in one command — the same way this issue's original defect was found.
failures.evidence: docs/kubernetes.md:1953-1955 reads "So a `printenv` run by `kubectl exec` into the container finds none of them, while one the role's own agent runs prints them." In this role container, PID 1 is the `legion launcher` the kubelet started from the container spec and the image config — the environment a `kubectl exec` inherits — and `tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/1/environ | grep '^PATH='` prints PATH=/opt/legion/bin:/opt/omp/bin:/opt/codegraph/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin, which is `/opt/legion/bin` first, exactly the value row 1 documents, and byte-identical to the shim's own rendered PATH (PID 10, same read). The cause is in the tree: the worker image's own ENV sets that PATH (packages/daemon/docker/worker.Dockerfile:526), and podPath's comment says so — "in the worker image it is the image PATH's first entry" (packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/manifest.go:1032-1035). The pod-spec half of the paragraph is right (testdata/golden/worker.json gives each role container env of POD_UID alone, and /proc/1/environ confirms it); only the conclusion drawn from it is wrong, and it is wrong about the one row an operator debugging a pod is most likely to check. kubectl is in the image but this pod's ServiceAccount cannot exec (`kubectl -n legion exec legion-infra-infra-212 -c tester -- printenv PATH` → `Error from server (Forbidden): ... cannot get resource "pods"`), so PID 1's environ is the container-side reading, which is the same environment. Pinned by the red test TestTheAgentEnvironmentParagraphNamesEveryVariableTheImageItselfSets in packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/agent_environment_doc_test.go (commit 4b8ffbdbf40e): `cd packages/daemon && go test -count=1 ./internal/runtime/sandbox/ -run TestTheAgentEnvironmentParagraphNamesEveryVariableTheImageItselfSets` fails with "...never names PATH, which the worker image's own ENV ... sets in every process of that container". The test is an accounting one, not a wording one: every variable the table lists that the image itself sets must be named in the paragraph. It goes green on the one-clause fix — probed by editing the sentence to "finds none of them but `PATH`, which the worker image's own `ENV` sets to the same value" and re-running it (ok 0.094s), then reverting with `jj restore docs/kubernetes.md`.

notes: Not a failure, but worth one line in the fix: the same paragraph cites packages/daemon/internal/config/kubernetes.go for refusing a runtime: kubernetes daemon 'without a Dispatch token and an Envoy token'. The composite claim is true, but only the Envoy rule is in that file (kubernetes.go:1353 requires envoy_token_file; it requires dispatch_url, and the Dispatch token rule is stage3.go:558-559, missingDispatchTokenFile, which fires because dispatch_url is set). A reader following the citation finds half of it.
